name: Hot-Blood Overdrive

gist.Tazune, the Angry Hot-Blood: The first two times each turn he would hurt himself with his own cards, nothing happens. Every recoil card in the deck is free on him and painful on anyone else.
gist.Phoenix Tackle: Big single-target burn that grows with Destruction Magic and hits its caster with recoil.
gist.Phoenix Bombardment: Drops a target to its last sliver of health, deals the same amount to the caster and ends the turn. On Tazune the price is waived.
gist.Last Resort: The caster deals twice its remaining health to one target and then dies. If that leaves no hero standing on either side, Willas wins.
gist.Angry Cheese: Hurts one of his heroes to search any Destruction spell.
gist.Victory Phoenix Cannon: Heavy single shot that lets him chain a cheap Destruction spell right after.
gist.Burning Finger: Plain single-target burn, stronger at higher Destruction Magic.
gist.Bomb Berserker Bartas: His cheap single-target spells may hit a second target afterwards. Low health.
gist.Luna, the Flame Fairy: Can use Firewall at any level, and her Firewall hits harder and burns your whole side, not just the attacker.
gist.Firewall: Face-down trap that burns whoever hits its hero; on Luna it sets your entire board on fire.
gist.Fireshield: Reaction: throws part of the damage back at the attacker.
gist.Unreasonable Anger: Reaction when hit: his next single-target hit is stronger.
gist.Booby Trap: Face-down trap that punishes the attacker.
gist.Golden Ankh: Revives a hero for one turn, usually Tazune for one more barrage.

plan: All gas. Willas levels Destruction Magic on Tazune and fires the biggest recoil spells in the game through him for free: Phoenix Tackle, Victory Phoenix Cannon into Burning Finger, Phoenix Bombardment to drop a hero to nothing. Angry Cheese finds whatever he wants. It is the fastest damage in the school for three or four turns, and it has no plan B: the deck has no creatures, no card draw worth the name, and when Tazune is frozen, stunned or dead the same spells chew up his other two heroes. Luna's Firewall is the one real trap he sets.

looks.early: Destruction Magic stacking on Tazune, an Angry Cheese already eaten, one face-down card on Luna.
looks.mid: Tazune casting twice a turn with smoke coming off him, Bartas and Luna hanging back at reduced health from paying for cheese.
looks.late: An exhausted hand, heroes scorched by their own recoil, Willas glaring at the top of his deck.

opening.tell: Tazune already wears two Destruction Magic; Bartas paid for an Angry Cheese with his own health.
opening.why: Everything runs through Tazune: a Snow Cannon on him or a hit that makes Willas spend a turn defending wastes cards that are worthless on his other heroes, whereas a slow setup just gives the fastest burn deck free turns.

midgame.tell: He controls no creatures; Tazune is the only hero without self-inflicted damage.
midgame.why: There is no board to clear, and his other two heroes have already been softened by his own costs, so focusing Tazune down ends the free recoil and with it the deck.

crisis.tell: Tazune is down or frozen and Luna has a card face-down; he is casting recoil spells from Bartas anyway.
crisis.why: Now every big spell costs him his own health, so staying alive (Cloud in a Bottle, Homerun!) wins by itself; charging into Luna's face-down Firewall is the one way to lose, because hers burns your whole side.

endgame.tell: His last heroes are low and he keeps fingering a card: Last Resort deals twice the caster's remaining health.
endgame.why: Last Resort is weak from a nearly dead hero but wins him a mutual wipe-out, so the answer is to finish the lowest hero now rather than give him a turn to line it up.
